mike_oncall:
seeing same from synthetic monitors. Auth service 95th latency jumped from 45ms -> 1.2s and error rate 401/403 spiked. tagging @alice_ng and @ben_platform.

hypothesis: rotation backfill job created new keys but didn't flush the in-memory key cache on a subset of auth instances (sticky caches). When client pools reuse long-lived connections to those instances, they still have old keys and reject new tokens, producing asymmetric behavior.

capturing followups: 
- add deterministic key-flush API in auth-service to force refresh per instance
- improve rotation job to do per-instance cache invalidation (kube exec or restart fallback)
- throttle client retries on 403 with exponential backoff and jitter

closing update — monitoring shows stable for 30m, no new customer escalations. Will keep incident open for the postmortem capture.

sre_anna:
dumps from auth-proxy show clients retrying quickly -> fanout to auth-service. DB auth_keys table read latency ↑ and a few DB connection pool saturations.

also seeing retry loop: client lib retries on 403 -> spikes request rate -> auth db read latency up -> more 403s as key lookups slow. It's a cascading retry amplification.

after first batch restart: error rate down by ~45%, auth latency dropping. DB p95 improved from 1.2s -> 220ms.

also recommend a canary phase next rotation: mark a cohort to accept both old and new kid for a short period (grace window) while monitoring kid_mismatch metrics.
